newsitem.title: USA: Bausch & Lomb says profits off, sets restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Bausch & Lomb says profits off, sets restructuring.

text.p: Bausch & Lomb Inc., a major maker of eye care products, said Wednesday earnings fell 85 percent in the latest quarter and that it will spend about $80 million on a major restructuring this year and next.
The company said it will reinvest expected annual savings of $100 million from the restructuring to bolster growth and provide a more predictable return for investors.
Bausch & Lomb said profits dipped to $3.3 million, or 6 cents a share, in the quarter ended on March 29 from $22.5 million, or 39 cents a share, in the 1996 period.

The company took a $12.8 million pretax charge in the quarter, and expects to recognise about $55 million to $60 million in restructuring costs by the end of 1997, most of which are expected to be recorded in the second quarter.
Bausch & Lomb also made a provision of $6.8 million after taxes for discontinuing sunglass product lines and for writing off its stake in a start-up technology venture.
The discontinued products, Ray-Ban sunglasses for driving and sports, compete in niche segments which the company said it believes can be reached more effectively through other brands.

Sales fell to $451.2 million from $469.3 miluion as the stronger dollar ate into revenues from other countries. On a constant dollar basis, Bausch & Lomb said revenues from ongoing operations rose 3 percent.

The restructuring is expected to result in improved operating margins, particularly in the company's eyewear business. The remainder of the savings will come from restructuring administrative functions, Bausch said.

The Rochester, N.Y.-based company said the savings were expected to be on top of savings of $50 million from restructuring projects announced early in 1996. The company said that these existing plans are on track.

Bausch & Lomb said it plans to phase out sunglass component manufacturing at its Frame Centre in Rochester and to "optimize" manufacturing operations in the sunglass global product delivery centres in San Antonio, Texas, Waterford, Ireland, and Hong Kong.

In response to a question at a news conference, Chief Executive William Carpenter said Bausch & Lomb was not seeking to divest its non-core businesses, which include Miracle Ear hearing aids; Charles River Laboratories, which raises animals for scientific experiments, and Curel, a maker of skin care lotion.
He said those units are independently managed and contribute to the company's first-quarter results.

Still, he said the company, which makes contact lenses and other optical products, might consider selling a non-core unit if it was worth more to another party. But he said Bausch & Lomb was not actively seeking buyers.

Bausch & Lomb's core businesses include contact lenses, lens care products, premium sunglasses and ophthalmic pharmaceutical products sold under the Bausch & Lomb, Arnette, Curel, SofLens66, Boston, Killer Loop and ReNu brand names. The company has 13,000 employees in 35 countries.
Bausch & Lomb stock rose $1 to $40.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
